verdict: OK to lend in Belagavi castings and forgings — Karnataka's GST and power demand are running well ahead of India, so back the auto and export-linked forging units with tight monthly discipline and stay away from single-customer, high-leverage foundries.
title: Belagavi castings & forgings: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Belagavi casting or forging unit melts scrap or buys billets, pours or hammers them into a component, machines it, and sells it to an OEM or a tier-1.** Cash comes in 30-90 days after dispatch; cash goes out for scrap, power, labour and freight almost immediately, so the working-capital cycle is the whole credit story. **Value sits in the customer approval and the tooling, not the furnace** — once a part is validated on a customer's line, pricing power is modest but the order is sticky. Capex is lumpy: a press, a furnace or a machining line. Collect from customer the melt capacity, the customer-wise order book and the scrap-to-finished yield before you size anything.

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is strong: Karnataka GST collections are up 11.1% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and state electricity demand is up 23.3% against India's 9.5% [D].** That power number matters directly — a foundry is an electricity-heavy business, so rising state demand tells you the industrial base around Belagavi is running. **India-wide, casting and forging output (NIC 24) is up 2.4% YoY and 3.4% Apr-to-date [D]** — real but modest growth, not a boom. **The local press coverage of the Belagavi and Belgaum foundry cluster is thin [1][2][3]**, so lean on first principles and on peers for this city.

## Peers tell you where the growth is
**Peer results split cleanly: forging and export-linked names are growing, commercial-vehicle-linked casting names are flat.** Ramkrishna Forgings grew revenue 54.9% YoY to Rs 1,405 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.23% and Rs 673 crore of new orders [6]; Happy Forgings carries a roughly Rs 950 crore order book with about 60% export-oriented [5] and grew quarterly revenue 20.4% [7]. **Nelcast's revenue fell to Rs 335 crore in Q2FY25 from Rs 362.6 crore, with the topline muted on subdued domestic and export CV demand [4]** — that is the segment to avoid. **On credit quality, the strong names run near-zero gearing [8], while a weaker caster sits at Crisil BB/Stable with Rs 72 crore of rated facilities [9]**; a forging peer improved Total Debt/GCA from 3.49x to 1.56x [10], and another caster held OPM at 8.4% with interest coverage of 3.8 times [11]. Pursue forging units with export or non-CV order books; avoid single-CV-customer foundries with thin margins.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the balance sheet.** Fund receivables and inventory through a cash credit or bill discounting line sized to the actual cycle, keep term debt only for a named machine with a customer order behind it, and take the promoter's personal guarantee. **Take every month: stock and receivable statements, the GST return, and the electricity bill** — the power bill is the cleanest output proxy for a foundry. Ask for customer-wise sales concentration; if one buyer is above a third of sales, ask for the contract and the payment history.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days stretching past the stated credit terms, and power consumption falling while sales are reported flat** — that gap means inventory is building or output is being misreported. If scrap payables start being paid late while receivables age, the unit is funding itself from suppliers and the cycle has broken.
watch: GST turnover falls below reported sales for two months -> ask for the sales register and re-rate the limit
Units fall while sales are flat -> inspect stock and confirm output before next disbursement
Top customer above a third of sales or days past terms -> seek the contract and reduce exposure
Supplier payments slipping past due -> treat as a liquidity warning and stop fresh limits
